alternatives_considered.approach: Expose GET /v1/meta/* HTTP endpoints for the reads
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The dashboard is server-rendered and can call the in-process adapter directly; new HTTP surface adds versioning and error-envelope work with no operator value in a read-first slice, and the issue names the contract as the JS interface behind src/integrations/meta_ads

alternatives_considered.approach: Persist synced Meta rows into SQLite derived_metrics
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Meta reads are raw source payloads owned by the provider, not derived metrics; persisting them now would mix raw and derived storage and break the TR-20 separation the foundation slice just established

work_order.approach: Add a versioned Meta adapter behind a typed read interface in src/integrations/meta_ads with the Graph version pinned to v26.0 per ADR-0004 in exactly one exported constant: index.js holds the contract (GRAPH_API_VERSION='v26.0' constant, typed shapes, error envelope, deterministic by-id sort, credential gating), fake.js implements the full interface with deterministic fixture data plus quota/revoked failure injection, and live.js implements the same interface over an injectable transport (constructor takes { token, fetchImpl } where fetchImpl defaults to globalThis.fetch; every request URL interpolates the pinned v26.0 version; 429/403 map to typed quota/permission errors; provider JSON is boundary-validated by parsing, never casting; secrets are never logged) and is only constructible for reads when META_ADS_ACCESS_TOKEN is present (otherwise it returns META_NOT_CONFIGURED without touching the network). The contract suite's live leg runs the live provider class with an injected test token and a stub fetchImpl serving canned v26.0 Graph-shaped JSON, so the identical shape/row-count/sort assertions run over both providers with zero business-logic changes and zero network (no real host is ever contacted). Extend the dashboard in src/web/pages.js with campaign regions (campaigns, ad sets, ads, insights tables with row counts and id sort) covering ideal, empty (existing no-connected-account checklist), loading (skeletons), partial (stale banner) and error (named failing check plus last-good timestamp plus Retry, prior rows preserved via a last-good snapshot passed in at render) states, and wire src/api/routes.js to construct the per-request fake provider and pass ?meta_error=quota|revoked through to renderPage. Cover with the adapter contract suite run identically against fake and stubbed-transport live plus dashboard region tests. Owner decision from plan/brief.md is followed: Meta end to end first; spec section 37 (Google-first wedge) is stale and overridden by that decision.
assumptions: Graph API pinned version is v26.0 per ADR-0004-direct-fetch-meta-adapter.md (accepted pin at brief time); the value is asserted by test, currency beyond the ADR is not asserted

No real Meta credentials exist in CI or QA, so the live path never touches the real network: CI exercises live reads against the stubbed transport (injected fetchImpl serving canned v26.0 Graph-shaped JSON) and exercises the credential gate as refusal
work_order.confidence_rationale: Adapter pattern, dashboard states, and test layout all already exist in the repo (fake-provider convention, five-state pages, node:test mirroring src/); the only new surface is the Meta read interface, which is read-only and credential-gated, and the single rejection point (v26.0 pin per ADR-0004) is now asserted by value in both the contract suite and AC-4.

files.change: Export GRAPH_API_VERSION='v26.0' single constant per ADR-0004, typed read interface (listCampaigns, listAdSets, listAds, getInsights), typed error envelope {code,message,details,retryable} with codes META_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED, META_PERMISSION_REVOKED, META_NOT_CONFIGURED, META_NETWORK, credential-gating helper, and deterministic by-id sort helper

FakeMetaAdsProvider implementing the full typed interface with deterministic fixture data (3 campaigns, ad sets, ads, insights with integer spend_micros), id-sorted output, and injectable failure modes ok|quota|revoked for tests and simulation

LiveMetaAdsProvider implementing the same interface over an injectable fetchImpl defaulting to globalThis.fetch, with the pinned v26.0 version interpolated into every request URL, env-credential gating (META_ADS_ACCESS_TOKEN), 429/403 mapped to typed quota/permission errors, boundary validation of provider JSON (parse, never cast), secrets never logged

Dashboard gains Meta campaign regions: campaigns, ad sets, ads and insights tables each with row counts and deterministic id sort; renderPage accepts { metaProvider, metaError } so ideal shows fake data with last-good sync timestamp, empty keeps the existing connect-Meta checklist, loading shows skeleton KPI/campaign cards without layout shift, partial shows stale-provider banner with age, error names the failing check (provider-sync/quota or provider-sync/permission), shows last-good timestamp, offers Retry button (focus moves to it), and preserves prior rows from the passed-in last-good snapshot; tables expose headers and row counts, single column under 900px

Page routes construct a per-request FakeMetaAdsProvider and pass request.query.state plus request.query.meta_error through to renderPage as { override, metaProvider, metaError }, so /?meta_error=quota|revoked drives the dashboard error panel with preserved rows

work_order.understanding: Issue #18 is the first Meta Ads slice of epic #14: a read-only Meta adapter (campaigns, ad sets, ads, insights) behind src/integrations/meta_ads with a fake provider for tests/simulation and a credential-gated live path, plus dashboard campaign regions with ideal/empty/loading/error states. Binding owner decision (plan/brief.md): Meta end to end first, Google Ads later, which overrides the Google-first argument in spec section 37. Depends on #16 (done): boot, SQLite repositories, five-state pages, and sdlc verbs all exist to build on. Rejection fix: pin GRAPH_API_VERSION to v26.0 per ADR-0004 (v24.0 in the prior plan was an unreasoned downgrade of the recorded pin) and assert the value, not just presence, in AC-4 and the contract suite.
